preconditions.description: The number of intersections n and roads m satisfy the given bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct valid intersections.
The path length k is within valid bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(path) == k and len(set(path)) == k and all(1 <= x <= n for x in path)
preconditions.description: The path contains k distinct valid intersections.

preconditions.expression: all((path[i], path[i+1]) in roads_set for i in range(k-1))
preconditions.description: Consecutive intersections in the path are connected by a road.
The graph is strongly connected (path exists between any pair of nodes).

postconditions.expression: min_rebuilds == sum(1 for i in range(k-1) if dist_to_t[path[i]] != dist_to_t[path[i+1]] + 1)
postconditions.description: The minimum rebuilds count steps where the next node in the path is not on any shortest path from the current node to t.

postconditions.expression: max_rebuilds == sum(1 for i in range(k-1) if dist_to_t[path[i]] != dist_to_t[path[i+1]] + 1 or (dist_to_t[path[i]] == dist_to_t[path[i+1]] + 1 and not is_on_some_shortest_path(path[i], path[i+1], t, dist_to_t, adj)))
postconditions.description: The maximum rebuilds count steps where the next node is either not on any shortest path, or is on a shortest path but the navigator could have chosen a different shortest path that does not include this node.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(min_rebuilds, int) and isinstance(max_rebuilds, int) and 0 <= min_rebuilds <= max_rebuilds <= k-1
postconditions.description: The output consists of two integers within the valid range of possible rebuilds.
